run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:03:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans on the proxy: ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR. At the alert anchor (2026-11-15T09:03:05Z) the rate was small (ingress 0.0148 spans/s, egress 0); it ramped sharply starting 09:12–09:13 (ingress error-span increase 0→54 per 60s) and at 09:20:00Z stood at 0.678/s (ingress) and 0.674/s (egress). The dominant cause traces one hop upstream: deployment checkout was rolled out at 09:11:43–09:11:46 to a new ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b whose container env sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, whereas the previous ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb used kafka:9092 and the kafka Service exposes only 9092/9093 (ClusterIP 100.66.162.182). The new checkout container logs 'dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', exhausts sarama brokers, exits with code 2 (reason Error) twice (09:15:21, 09:18:48), is CrashLoopBackOff/not Ready, and the deployment reports MinimumReplicasUnavailable. frontend then records its own error spans on POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder at the same 0.6778/s rate, and frontend-proxy logs show 'POST /api/checkout ... 500 - via_upstream' from the frontend. A second, lower-rate failure mode predates the rollout: 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on frontend SSR routes (/api/products/*, /api/recommendations) seen from ~08:55 to ~09:09; its cause is not established and frontend logs were empty, so it remains an open hypothesis. Kafka itself is not shown to be failing (pod Ready, 0 restarts, normal KRaft logs; accounting and fraud-detection still point at kafka:9092).

claims.text: At the alert anchor 2026-11-15T09:03:05Z frontend-proxy had error spans only on operation 'ingress' (rate 0.014814815 spans/s) and none on 'router frontend egress' (0), while unset-status spans were 12.49/s (ingress) and 12.5/s (egress).
At 2026-11-15T09:20:00Z frontend-proxy error-span rates were 0.6777778/s on span_name 'ingress' and 0.674074/s on span_name 'router frontend egress' (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR).

The frontend-proxy ingress error-span 60s increase went from 6 at 09:12:05Z to 54 at 09:13:05Z and stayed between 54 and 92 per minute through 09:21:05Z, while before 09:12:05Z it was only 0–6 per minute (sporadic, starting 08:53:05Z).

Deployment otel-demo/checkout is at revision 2 with replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-15T09:18:49Z); its checkout container env includes KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999.

The superseded ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, while the active ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 — i.e. the pod-template Kafka address changed in the rollout.

Kubernetes events record the checkout rollout at 09:11:43–09:11:46Z ('Scaled up replica set checkout-849d65649b from 0 to 1', 'Scaled down replica set checkout-5dccddf8bb from 1 to 0', 'Created pod: checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz') and a Warning BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout' at 2026-11-15T09:18:49Z.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz (created 2026-11-15T09:11:43Z, owner ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b) has container 'checkout' Ready=false, restarts=1, lastState terminated with exitCode 2 and reason Error at 09:15:21Z, and current state terminated with exitCode 2 reason Error at 09:18:48Z; pod Ready condition is False (ContainersNotReady) since 09:18:49Z.

The checkout container log (current instance, 09:11:45Z–09:20:04Z) repeatedly shows 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', 'client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to' and finally 'kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', after which it logs 'starting to listen on tcp: "[::]:8080"' (09:13:46Z, 09:17:23Z) and restarts.
Service otel-demo/kafka is a ClusterIP service with clusterIP 100.66.162.182 and only two ports: 'plaintext' 9092→9092 and 'controller' 9093→9093; no port 9999 is exposed.

The kafka deployment env shows the broker configured for PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092 with listeners PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093; only the checkout deployment uses kafka:9999, while accounting and fraud-detection use kafka:9092.

frontend records its own error spans during the outage at exactly the proxy's rate: at 09:20:00Z 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'POST' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' each had STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0.6777778/s, plus 'tcp.connect' 0.0741/s; all of these were 0 at 09:03:05Z.

frontend-proxy access log for 09:15:24Z–09:16:27Z shows repeated 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' records (upstream cluster 'frontend'), i.e. the proxy relayed an upstream 500, not its own 503.

Before the rollout, frontend-proxy access log 08:55:27Z–09:09:13Z shows sporadic '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses on frontend SSR routes (GET /api/products/…, /api/recommendations?…) interleaved with 200s.

The failure chain is visible in traces: a failing request is load-generator 'GET' (error=true, http.status_code 503) → frontend-proxy 'ingress' (error=true, http.status_code 503) → frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error="true", http.status_code "0"), and frontend-proxy exposes only the operations 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client).
Checkout worked before the change: frontend-proxy logged 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 200 - via_upstream' at 09:01:31Z, i.e. the 500s on /api/checkout start only after the 09:11:43Z rollout.

frontend-proxy itself is running and not restarting: pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c created 08:38:24Z, container Ready=true, restarts=0, started 08:38:28Z; frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv is likewise Ready=true with restarts=0.

Container memory does not explain the failures: over the whole window the frontend container's max working set was 130,068,480 bytes against a 209,715,200-byte limit (≈62%), and the checkout container's max was 9,817,112 bytes against 536,870,912 bytes.

Rejected: a kafka broker failure. The kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh (created 08:38:24Z) is Running and Ready with restarts=0, its log shows normal KRaft metadata/snapshot activity through 09:20Z, and other kafka clients (accounting, fraud-detection) are configured with kafka:9092 rather than the unreachable 9999 port.

The checkout KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 points at the kafka Service ClusterIP on a port the Service does not map (only 9092/9093), so the connect attempts are dropped (i/o timeout) instead of being refused; the container then exits with code 2 when its Kafka producer cannot be initialised, keeping checkout unavailable and driving frontend /api/checkout 500s and frontend-proxy error spans.

The alert's first firing at 09:03:05Z (about 8 minutes before the checkout rollout) was most likely triggered by the sporadic frontend 503 UC connection resets on /api/products and /api/recommendations, since the alert's stated condition is 'above 0' and ingress error spans existed from 08:53:05Z; the checkout outage then sustained and amplified the error rate.

gaps: No alerting or recording rule named RequestErrorRate (nor any rule) is loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data twice), so the alert's exact PromQL expression, evaluation window and threshold are unverified, and the annotation value 'current: 1.7333333333333332' could not be reproduced from the available series (observed frontend-proxy error-span rates were 0.0148/s at 09:03:05Z and 0.678/s at 09:20:00Z).

Jaeger returned no traces for the 09:12–09:20Z outage window (traces_search_by_tags error=true for frontend-proxy in 09:16–09:19Z and for frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder in 09:12–09:20Z both returned no_data), and the available sample ends around 09:00Z, so the full trace graph of the failing checkout calls was not inspected.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 08:45–09:15Z (0 lines read), so the frontend-side error text behind the /api/checkout 500s and behind the 503 UC resets is unknown.
Who or what applied checkout deployment revision 2 at 09:11:43Z is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
The cause of the sporadic upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} 503s on frontend SSR routes is not established; frontend itself emitted no error spans for those requests.
Error-span metric series end at 09:21:05Z (last sample), so the frontend-proxy error rate after that time is unknown.
Whether the sporadic frontend 503 resets existed before 08:51–08:53Z is unknown, since the status_code=ERROR series for frontend-proxy only begins in that period.
next_steps: Inspect the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule definition for RequestErrorRate to confirm its expression and threshold, since it is not present in the queried Prometheus.

Restore checkout's Kafka address to the Service port that exists (kafka:9092, as in ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb) or publish port 9999 on the kafka Service, then roll the deployment and confirm the checkout pod becomes Ready and /api/checkout returns 200 again.
Find out who applied checkout deployment revision 2 at 09:11:43Z and whether the KAFKA_ADDR change was intentional.
Investigate the sporadic frontend upstream_reset_before_response_started 503s on /api/products and /api/recommendations separately from the checkout outage.
